evidence_note: The controlled response retains the representational-behavioural gap but omits most layer-wise, data, ablation and task-specific diagnostics; its fine-tuning recommendation also shifts the proposed next step.

The controlled response preserves the central warning that translation quality, cultural mismatch, annotation and tokenization can distort capability comparisons, although it omits several validation procedures and artifact categories.

Both responses preserve the same causal diagnostic—inspect segmentation and test alternative tokenization under controlled conditions—although the naive response adds explicit controls, probing and qualitative error analysis.

The controlled response retains human evaluation and common limitations but materially narrows the naive response's multi-method strategy combining reference-free metrics, human judgment and downstream evidence.
Both responses use replication across seeds, models and prompts or tasks as the central robustness test, while the naive response adds statistical uncertainty, controls and layer-wise diagnostics.
Both responses check major pipeline components, but the controlled response omits the intermediate-output tracing needed to localise where the discrepancy first appears.

Both responses propose intervening through ablation or counterfactual modification and measuring behavioural change, although the naive response adds mediation analysis and necessary-versus-sufficient causal framing.

Both responses investigate preprocessing, tokenization, metric alignment and model outputs before reporting cautiously; the naive response adds replication, training-data analysis and alternative validation methods.
